clue.text: Heard about jumper's trick

indicators.note: what is heard about is what reaches the ear, so the word for the jumper is taken by its sound

parts.note: a jumper here is a roo, a kangaroo; the possessive roo's is said the same way

explanation.surface: Gossip about a sweater turns out to be a deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater, but it is the bounding kangaroo, ROO; ROO'S said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a ruse is a cunning stratagem meant to deceive.

clue.text: Again play part for peace

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again, as in redo
to pose is to play a part, pretending to be someone

explanation.surface: An actor performs a role a second time in the interests of harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: repose is rest and calm, a state of quiet tranquillity.

clue.text: They don't count second shopping centre group: resistance follows

indicators.note: follows places the resistance letter after everything before it

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
a bee is a gathering of people for a joint activity, such as a spelling bee
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A list of items about a mall's management, with a protest group following on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural in sense: small beer means things of no importance, matters that do not count.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for trivial matters, so unimportant things are considered not to count.

clue.text: Risking jewellery after school?

indicators.note: after puts the jewellery word behind the school word

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Wearing expensive jewellery out after school could be a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but a GAM, a school of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: gambling means taking a chance, putting something at stake.

clue.text: Knowing the writer's back catalogue?

parts.note: arch means knowing or slyly playful
the writer refers to the setter, so 'the writer's' (writer has) gives I'VE

explanation.surface: A knowing author looking back over a list of past work.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is 'the writer', so 'the writer has' gives I'VE; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of past records, a playful sort of catalogue of the past.

clue.text: Peace for now ably, no end, negotiated, with help of this?

definitions.text: Peace for now ably, no end, negotiated, with help of this?

indicators.note: negotiated suggests terms worked through and rearranged, so the letters before it are reordered
no end says the final letter of the word ably is dropped

explanation.surface: Diplomats ask whether a temporary peace was skilfully negotiated thanks to some equilibrium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims ABLY to ABL; PEACE, FOR, NOW and ABL are then rearranged by 'negotiated'. The whole clue also describes how such peace is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance of power is an equilibrium between states in which no single nation dominates, often credited with keeping peace.

clue.text: Day in Rome, time that is in local parlance

parts.note: the Ides was a day in the Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: A visitor to Rome learns the local way of saying a date and time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'local parlance' is Latin, the language of Rome mentioned earlier, in which these words mean 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase, abbreviated i.e., used to introduce an explanation in the sense of namely.

clue.text: Feminist about to stop working seen as comparatively selfish?

indicators.note: about means the feminist's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist author of The Female Eunuch
a machine that stops working is said to die

explanation.surface: A feminist about to quit her job is judged rather self-centred.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: more grasping, wanting more for oneself than others, hence more selfish.

clue.text: Agreement about being put forward for election taking only some people in?

indicators.note: about means the agreement word wraps around the election word

parts.note: a deal is an agreement
a nomination is the act of being put forward as a candidate

explanation.surface: A deal is struck about a candidacy, with only some voters involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a denominational school or church takes in only members of one religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: Denominational means tied to one religious sect, so such an institution admits only certain believers.

clue.text: Means of communication in Alabama port

definitions.meaning: a ... phone, used for calls and texts
A port city on the Gulf coast of Alabama

explanation.surface: Telephone lines in a Southern harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone is a mobile in British usage, and Mobile is also a city in Alabama.

clue.text: Locate branch office — it does nothing!

parts.note: to place something is to locate it
BO is the abbreviation for branch office

explanation.surface: A complaint that finding a local branch office is a pointless exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active ingredient, so it has no real medical effect.

clue.text: Porter admitting cricket side in school

indicators.note: admitting means letting the cricket word inside the porter's name

parts.note: Cole Porter was the American songwriter
the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the other being the off side

explanation.surface: A school doorman lets in a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman but is Cole Porter. In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind a right-handed batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a place of education, a sense of school, as in a college of art.

clue.text: Final episode not changed showing stubbornness

indicators.note: changed tells us these three words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer refuses to alter the last instalment of a series, digging their heels in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-opinionated holds rigidly to their own views, which is a stubborn quality.

clue.text: Dog seen in gym, family facility, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the words are heard, so their sound gives the spelling

parts.note: gym is PE (physical education), family is KIN and facility is EASE; together PE KIN EASE

explanation.surface: A dog was spotted at a leisure centre with family-friendly amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: Facility in the sense of ease, as in doing something with facility.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pekinese is a small long-haired toy breed of dog originally from China.

clue.text: Remove worker, a sexist to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A call to sack a staff member who is partly sexist.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to erase is to wipe out or delete something.

clue.text: Introduction of Australian TV series, new, displaying confidence

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter
new means the letters of the words before it are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The opening of a fresh Australian television series shows self-assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being assertive means confidently stating one's views, so it shows self-assurance.

clue.text: European region for example in political group

indicators.note: in puts the example word inside the political group

parts.note: a caucus is a group within a political party
as means for example, as in 'cities, as Paris'

explanation.surface: A sample region within a party faction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caucasus is the mountainous area between the Black and Caspian Seas, on Europe's edge.

clue.text: Halls test cut short after article

indicators.note: after puts the shortened test behind the article

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: cut short says the final letter of the test word is removed

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: School halls where an exam is stopped early after a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are entrance halls or central courts in buildings, the plural of atrium.

clue.text: One living in bowl getting new start? He shows little emotion

indicators.note: getting new start means the first letter of the bowl creature is swapped for another

parts.note: a goldfish is the classic pet kept in a bowl

explanation.surface: A pet fish given a fresh beginning, but someone unmoved by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not clued; the definition fixes it as C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold fish is an idiom for an aloof, unfeeling person.

clue.text: National character from Athens list

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A Greek character from a roster of citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chilean is a citizen of Chile, a national of that South American country.

clue.text: Secure metal carriage

parts.note: to land something is to secure it, as with a deal or a fish
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A metal fixing fastened to a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with a folding top.

clue.text: Something Communist does? Work in publishing maybe

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a ... is something done by a Communist
to edit a text for publication, often by cutting sensitive parts

explanation.surface: A question about what a Communist gets up to, and a job in books.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to edit or censor a document for publication.

clue.text: Crash out of this?

parts.note: a crash is what results from a path heading straight for impact with another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash out' suggests falling asleep or being eliminated, but read plainly a crash comes out of this path.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision course is a trajectory that will lead to an impact unless changed, so a crash follows from it.

clue.text: Abandon holiday

definitions.meaning: to desert or walk away from

explanation.definitionFit: To leave is to desert someone, and leave is also authorised time away from a job.

clue.text: Toast entails being relaxed

indicators.note: being relaxed means the letters loosen up and settle into a new order

explanation.surface: A toast that comes with a laid-back attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Sláinte is a Gaelic toast, used in Ireland and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking salute meaning health, said when raising a glass, like cheers.

clue.text: Mother back with Heather in the country

indicators.note: back means the word for mother is turned around

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: Mum returns with a friend called Heather to live in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant, whose genus is Erica.
explanation.definitionFit: America is often called simply the country by people living there, the United States.

clue.text: Female extremely tactful with island group

parts.note: she is a female pronoun

indicators.note: extremely picks out the two extreme letters of the word that follows

parts.note: and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A diplomatic woman with a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Shetland is the archipelago north of mainland Scotland.

clue.text: Old Bob in sulk becoming a nuisance

indicators.note: in puts the shilling letter inside the sulk word

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'
a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: An old man named Bob sulks and becomes irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is old British slang for a shilling, the coin worth 5p, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a person or thing that annoys, an irritant.
